units.text: 8. Keeping the spec current
The spec is dated beside its title. A claim is only as current as the date its source was read, and prices, terms and neighbors are the first to drift.
What to re-check, and when
When this happens
Re-check
Spec sections
GitHub changes Actions prices, runner sizes, limits or terms
Pass 1, items 1 and 2; the github/docs and github/site-policy repositories
9.2 to 9.5; risk 1
Anthropic changes its plans, claude-code-action's sign-in, bare mode or its legal page
Pass 1, item 3
9.4 and 9.5; risks 2 and 3; R6
symphony-protocol publishes a release (0.5.0 is next)
Its release notes and validation/known.json
2 (maturity); risks 6, 12 and 13
A neighbor ships: gh-aw's queue leaves its draft design record, unsorry, Copilot's agents, openai/symphony
The worksheet in section 5, for that tool
4, 5 and 8
A research question meets its acceptance criteria: R1's full run, R3's measurement pass, R4 on the canary
The question's own criteria
Beethoven builds a gate, or its launcher reaches a second university
The repository at its new commit
2 and 5.2; claims U4 to U6; risk 8
You lift the grant-data hold
Nothing to research; the grant reviewers' version in section 6 changes
Before any outside use: a submission, a talk, a public page
Pass 1 again if the spec's date is more than a month old (a default; change it if you like)
9, and every claim quoted
How to ask for an update
Post this in the project chat, with the link or the text of what changed:
Update the taxonomy spec: <what changed, with a link>. Re-grade the claims it touches, update the parts of the manual that rest on them, and tell me in the thread what changed.

The thread that makes the change writes its notes under research/taxonomy/notes/ (a new file for a new topic, or lines in the topic's file), puts adversarial checks under research/taxonomy/verify/, and moves the date beside the spec's title.
9. Glossary
Term
Meaning
Apptainer
A container runtime for clusters that runs without administrator rights
Blackboard
A shared store that independent agents read and write; the classic AI architecture (Nii, 1986)
Board
The file STATE.md on the branch board, which board.yml rewrites from the issues, branches, claim files and pull requests; nobody edits it by hand
Claim
The push that creates the branch claude/N for issue N, whose first commit adds a claim file naming the worker, the plan and the files to touch
CLAIM
The Checklist for Artificial Intelligence in Medical Imaging, updated in 2024 (Radiology: Artificial Intelligence)
claude-code-action
Anthropic's GitHub Action, anthropics/claude-code-action, which runs Claude Code inside a workflow
Compare-and-swap
An update that succeeds only if the value is still what the writer last saw; git applies one to a ref on every push
Coordinator
The deterministic steps in the board's run that release idle claims and announce overlaps, and Claude in coordinator.yml, which plans epics into tasks
CrossHair, Z3
A tool that searches by symbolic execution for inputs that break a Python function's contracts, and the solver it uses
Epic
An issue that asks for more than one piece of work, which the coordinator plans into tasks
Fast-forward
A push that only adds commits on top of the branch's tip, which git accepts without force
Fencing token
A number that rises with each grant of a lock, so a resource can refuse a holder whose lease has expired
Five-hour window, weekly limit
The usage limits of a Claude plan, shared by everything that runs on it
gh-aw
GitHub Agentic Workflows (github/gh-aw), which compiles agent workflows written in Markdown into Actions; its work queue is Symphony's closest neighbor
GITHUB_TOKEN
The token GitHub gives each workflow run, scoped to its repository, with 1,000 API requests an hour
icontract
A Python library for contracts (preconditions, postconditions, invariants) on functions
Interleaving
One order in which the steps of several concurrent workers can happen
Lease

In distributed systems, a lock that expires unless renewed (Gray and Cheriton, 1989). In git, --force-with-lease is a forced push that succeeds only if the remote branch is still where the pusher expects
Mutant
A copy of the code with one deliberate fault; a check that does not catch it does not bite
Open OnDemand
A web portal to a university cluster, through which Beethoven starts its jobs
Oracle
An independent statement of the right outcome, here written from the spec's text, against which every interleaving is checked
Overlap
Two pieces of open work that change the same file; the board lists them in the order they should land
PreToolUse hook
A command Claude Code runs before a tool call, which can refuse the call
Push guard
tools/guard_push.py, a PreToolUse hook that refuses forbidden pushes before they run, on the worker's own machine
REFORMS
Consensus recommendations for science that uses machine learning (Kapoor et al., Science Advances, 2024), 32 items
Release
What happens to a claim with no commit for 24 hours: its labels come off, a comment says what the branch holds, and the branch is renamed released/N-sha, so the work is kept and the name is free
Remote Control
Claude Code's feature that lets a session running on one machine be driven from claude.ai or the Claude app
Required check
A status check that a ruleset makes pass before anything merges; Symphony's is named check
Ruleset
GitHub's rules for branches or tags, such as required checks, blocked force pushes or a merge queue, set for a repository or an organization
Safe outputs
gh-aw's way of letting an agent ask for a write, such as a pull request or a comment, that a separate job with write permission carries out
Slurm, sbatch
The cluster's batch scheduler, and its command for submitting a job
Standard runner
A GitHub-hosted virtual machine of the default size; free and unlimited on public repositories
Stigmergy
Coordination through traces left in a shared environment, as Symphony's agents coordinate through branches and labels rather than messages
Subscription token
CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN, made by claude setup-token, which lets claude-code-action bill a person's Claude plan instead of an API key
TRIPOD+AI
The reporting guideline for clinical prediction models that use regression or machine learning (BMJ, 2024)
Worker
Anything that claims issues: a person's sessions, a routine, or an agent in GitHub Actions, each labelled worker:name
